headline: Bond Selloff and Rate-Hike Fears Cloud the Open as Breadth Stays Lopsided
body_html:
Futures point to a cautious open on Thursday after Wednesday's session left broad damage across the coverage universe: 345 names declined against just 197 advancers out of 545 tracked, with seven of eight sectors finishing in the red. Homebuilders led the retreat with a 2.28% sector loss, followed by Healthcare off 1.39% and Materials down 1.29% — a pattern consistent with rising-rate anxiety rather than any single idiosyncratic shock.

The macro backdrop has sharpened overnight. New York Fed President Williams characterized another rate hike before year-end as 'reasonable,' a remark that is reverberating through the bond market, which was already selling off ahead of an anticipated meeting between Presidents Trump and Xi. Gold slipped as Treasury yields and oil prices climbed in tandem, while the Indian rupee fell to a one-week low on compounding rate-hike worries. Shipping data showed traffic through the Strait of Hormuz running below its ten-day average, keeping energy-supply questions alive.

Cybersecurity was the standout pocket of Wednesday's strength — Palo Alto Networks gained 5.0% and CrowdStrike added 4.97% — and that momentum will be worth watching at the open. Geopolitically, Netanyahu's UN address and a Democratic war-powers vote in Washington are potential intraday catalysts that traders should keep on their screens.

briefs.headline: Fed's Williams Flags Year-End Rate Hike as 'Reasonable'
briefs.body: New York Fed President John Williams said Wednesday that an additional interest-rate increase before year-end is a reasonable expectation, adding institutional weight to a bond market already in selloff mode. The comment landed as Treasury yields pushed higher, amplifying pressure on rate-sensitive sectors such as Homebuilders, which dropped 2.28% in Wednesday's session.

briefs.headline: Bond Market Selloff Deepens Ahead of Trump-Xi Meeting
briefs.body: Sovereign debt continued to slide overnight as investors position cautiously before a high-stakes meeting between the U.S. and Chinese presidents. The combination of elevated yields and geopolitical uncertainty is dampening risk appetite broadly, with the rupee sliding to a one-week low and gold retreating as competing assets draw capital away from traditional havens.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Traffic Slips Below Ten-Day Average, Oil Questions Linger
briefs.body: Data tracking vessel movements through the Strait of Hormuz shows throughput running below the ten-day average, sustaining uncertainty about regional crude supply. Asia's oil imports hit a post-conflict high in September but remained historically subdued, a combination that analysts say keeps upward pressure on global energy prices and complicates central-bank inflation calculus.

briefs.headline: Cybersecurity Names Dominate Wednesday's Leaderboard
briefs.body: Palo Alto Networks surged 5.0% and CrowdStrike added 4.97% to lead the broader market on Wednesday, with identity-software name Okta not far behind at 4.45%. The cluster of gains suggests fresh institutional rotation into cybersecurity as enterprises continue spending on network defense, a theme traders will watch for follow-through at Thursday's open.

briefs.headline: Netanyahu UN Visit Adds Geopolitical Layer to Morning Trade
briefs.body: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's brief appearance in New York for the UN General Assembly, widely expected to include pointed remarks about U.S.-Israel relations, landed against a backdrop of a Democratic war-powers vote in Congress with some Republican defections on Iran policy. Geopolitical headlines from Turtle Bay could trigger short-term volatility in energy and defense-adjacent names.

briefs.headline: Sarepta and Vital Farms Lead Wednesday's Decliners
briefs.body: Sarepta Therapeutics fell 8.94% to pace the day's losers, dragging on an already weak Healthcare sector that closed down 1.39%. Premium food producer Vital Farms shed 8.36%, while SolarEdge dropped 7.57%, extending a difficult stretch for the solar segment. The breadth of Wednesday's declines — 345 names lower — underscores how broadly the risk-off tone was felt.
